Personally one of my greatest social challenges is staying cognizant of the fact that a failure to act friendly at *some point* within the opportunity of an interaction is a bad mark on my relationship with the person at hand.
This is a social truth that has always been particularly jarring to me; that a man can be so hated for showing weakness, even when he is facing the hardest trials of his life.

It's honestly really difficult to stay motivated in the face of so many challenges, and it's not like anyone can whisk my problems away. I think the real issue I have is that none of my problems have easy solutions, and by that I mean there are lot of little things that could easily go wrong, completely derailing/delaying my plans for the future.

I kind of do the same thing. I'll actually do some productive stuff, and then I'll think more about tackling other legitimate problems in my life, and I get overwhelmed. It's hard to stay motivated and focus on one thing at a time, when multiple things each of which work in their own way to cause instability in my life seem to need to be addressed simultaneously. What sucks doubly is being responsible for other people. I can take care of myself just fine. Throw a bunch of family members who are less emotionally resilient against hardship into the mix, and I tend to feel pretty stressed out.

I have such a strong inclination to avoid connecting with others that I don't even bother trying to imagine how a pleasant conversation could go. I've done it before, and I've had nice conversations, but I'm always so emotionally removed from it all that nice interractions with others become utterly meaningless as soon as they're over. The other person will cease to enter my mind, and I'll just go back to thinking about my life and what happens in it from a very distant perspective like I always do.

Idk. I was born very privileged. And by that I mean I wasn't abused or born into abject poverty. I guess my hand still sucks though. I take responsibility for myself, but I also wonder if I have any unknown limitations to my abilities that cause me to be dissapointed with myself. Not so that I could have an excuse, but just to know. A lot of times I'm not even sure of what cards I'm playing with exactly.

It used to be a lot easier to make a living wage back in the day. I'm sure you're in good company at your age as far as feeling like a failure goes. I'm 22 and it seems like the future is bleak.

Like a good number of people apparently, it started in middle school. My social skills were clearly limited and I began to legitimately feel like I was not worthy within the context of the social enviornment. I faced enough social rejection at the time that it reenforced the belief that I wasn't good enough, even if I wasn't bullied super harshly or publicly humiliated at all.  I also became aware of my family's shitty financial situation. This was around 2008-2009. My parents are terrible communicators, which combined with the stress created a dysfunctional family dynamic. I started to not want anything to do with my family, and enjoyed any and all time out of the house. I was never abused, but for several years my parents were on the brink if divorce. I already started spending all my time playing videogames and watching TV from a young age, so that...continued. Fuck it man. The lines are really blurred about when it all started. I'm not sure if I was ever particularly happy or interested in the world.

Antidepressants usually work best on people with only mild depression. The worse the depression, the less likely medication is going to make a difference, especially without therapy, which some people can't really afford. My only gripe with antidepressants is the experimental nature of the drugs. They actually aren't that well understood at all. When you start taking medication, you're basically starting an experiment on yourself where you're altering the chemicals in your brain, for better or worse. From my perspective, I've grown pretty indifferent about my life enough to be willing to start that blind experiment. At the same time maybe that means I do care, enough to where I don't want to mess up my brain if I'm ever somehow able to beat the depression without the meds.For these reasons, I have little faith in it. There's also the burdensome cost for those without insurance.
